_why: Shared corpus for the company/role matching key (#2666). The core's normalizeTextKey (tracker-parse.mjs) is the source of truth; web/src/lib/core/normalize-text-key.mjs is a declared copy that exists because the browser cannot reach the user's checkout. This file is the single list both sides are checked against — two lists would drift, which is the whole failure this corpus guards.
_note: Expected values are NOT hand-written: the assertion derives them from the core and compares the mirror against that. The strings below are the cases; the core decides the answers.

cases.why: accented Latin — the plain case the ASCII-only key destroyed (nestl)
same name in NFD (macOS stores filenames decomposed) — must key identically to the NFC form
umlaut plus a second word
the collision that started this: the old key made it 'koda', matching a different company called Koda and hiding a real opening
Portuguese cedilla and tilde
CJK — the old key emptied it, so it never matched and duplicated forever
the counterpart of the collision: must stay DISTINCT from Škoda

Polish z with a dot ABOVE, precomposed. The dot is a letter the user typed, so this must stay DISTINCT from 'Zubr' — and it is the case that was missing when the Turkish fix landed: an NFD-then-strip implementation decomposed it and collapsed the two. Structural protection: NFKC keeps ż as ONE code point the dot-strip cannot reach, unlike i + U+0307, which has no precomposed form.
the counterpart: must stay DISTINCT from Żubr
Lithuanian e with a dot above, same class as Żubr and same reason: two dotted letters the user typed, not a casing artifact. Must stay DISTINCT from 'Eme'.
the counterpart: must stay DISTINCT from Ėmė
Maltese g with a dot above. Must stay DISTINCT from 'Generali', which is a different (and real) company — the collision this class would cause is not hypothetical.
the counterpart: must stay DISTINCT from Ġenerali
fullwidth Latin, routine in Japanese-sourced data — NFKC folds it to acme
fi ligature — NFKC decomposes it

Turkish dotted capital I. toLowerCase yields i + U+0307, and that combining mark used to survive into the key, so this did NOT match 'Istanbul Tekstil' even though the two read identically on screen. Decision reversed 12-ago-2026 after the same artifact turned up in a third surface and, worse, inside verify-pipeline's duplicate check, where it produced a false green. The targeted fix now strips U+0307 after lowercasing, so İstanbul/Istanbul match. It is scoped to the artifact CASING CREATES: Škoda != Skoda, Nestlé != Nestle, Zürich != Zurich and İŞ BANKASI != Is Bankasi all still hold, because those marks are letters the user typed. This key is a frozen contract surface the web derives from, so the mirror in web/src/lib/core/normalize-text-key.mjs changed in the same commit and test-all §55.7 compares them.
plain ASCII control — must be unaffected by any of the above
nullish must key to empty string, not the literal 'null' (which made null and undefined match each other)
empty stays empty
runs of separators and surrounding whitespace collapse and trim
